facts.statement: The genus Pseudorhina was described by Jaekel in 1898.
The classification of Pseudorhina was revised by Klug and Kriwet in 2012.
Pseudorhina is currently considered the oldest known genus of angel shark.
facts.quote: Pseudorhina is currently the oldest known angel shark genus.

facts.statement: The genus Pseudorhina is placed in the monotypic family Pseudorhinidae.
facts.quote: has been placed in a monotypic family called Pseudorhinidae

facts.statement: Fossils of Pseudorhina are known from the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous periods of Europe.
facts.quote: Fossils are known from the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous of Europe.

facts.statement: The species P. acanthoderma and P. alifera are distinguished by differences in body size, proportions, and tooth anatomy.
facts.quote: Pseudorhina acanthoderma and Pseudorhina alifera from the Late Jurassic of Europe, which are known from full body remains, are distinguished from each other by having a different body sizes, proportions, as well as differences in tooth anatomy

facts.statement: The species P. acanthoderma and P. alifera are known from full body fossils in the Late Jurassic Solnhofen Plattenkalk limestones of southern Germany.
facts.quote: The fully body species P. acanthoderma and P. alifera are known from the Late Jurassic Solnhofen Plattenkalk limestones of southern Germany.

facts.statement: The time range for Pseudorhina is from the Toarcian to the Valanginian, between 182.9 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Valanginian (182.9 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Pseudorhina belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
